newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI sees turnaround in non-food bank credit.
newsitem.headline: India RBI sees turnaround in non-food bank credit.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Wednesday said it saw a turnaround in banks's credit flow to the commercial sector.
"On the basis of the revised data for March 28, 1997, the decline in non-food credit between March 28, 1997 and June 20, 1997, was to the tune of 40.64 billion rupees," it said in a statement.
"When compared with a decline of 72.20 billion rupees in the corresponding period last year, there has been a turnaround of 31.56 billion rupees," it said.

"While non-food bank credit declined by 40.64 billion rupees in the first quarter of 1997/98, banks' investment in commercial paper, bonds/debentures/shares of public sector undertakings and private corporate sector and bills rediscounted have shown a large increase of 26.82 billion rupees as compared with a modest increase of 8.70 billion rupees in the corresponding period last year," RBI said.

"The total flow of funds from scheduled commercial banks to commercial sector thus shows a decline of 13.82 billion rupees in the first quarter of 1997/98 as compared with a large decline of 63.50 billion rupees in the first quarter of 1996/97."
The RBI said the decline in non-food bank credit in the first quarter this year has been the lowest in the comparable periods between 1993/94 and 1997/98.
The decline was 66.44 billion rupees in 1993/94, 91.36 billion rupees in 1994/95, 60.70 billion rupees in 1995/96 and 72.20 billion rupees in 1996/97.
